heroHeadline: Xiang Yang Hong 33 Day 18 Near Pag-asa; AFP Warns Philippines in 'Political, Economic, and Informational War' Over WPS — UNCLOS Silence Day 13
heroSubtitle: China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 continued its unauthorized presence in the Kalayaan Island Group near Pag-asa (Thitu) Island for an 18th consecutive day on May 24, 2026, as Beijing's diplomatic silence on the Philippines' UNCLOS Article 246 note verbale extended to a 13th consecutive day — the longest unanswered Philippine diplomatic instrument in the Marcos administration's West Philippine Sea dispute history. AFP Deputy Chief of Staff Lieutenant General Arvin Lagamon warned May 24 that 'we are already at war — not yet a kinetic war, but the political war, the economic war, and more importantly, the cyber and informational war are already going on.' WPS Spokesperson Rear Admiral Roy Trinidad declared that 'the modern battlefield is the mindset of the Filipino people,' warning that Chinese information operations targeting Philippine media and public opinion represent a deliberate cognitive warfare campaign. The Philippines' three-front West Philippine Sea standoff persisted: (1) Xiang Yang Hong 33 near Pag-asa (Day 18; PCG formal investigation into the May 16-17 Chinese personnel landing on Sandy Cay 2 and Sandy Cay 3 ongoing); (2) Scarborough Shoal 'marine nature reserve' declaration — DFA protest of May 11 unanswered; (3) Second Thomas Shoal — BRP Sierra Madre marine garrison facing continued CCG blockade posture. On May 23, the Philippine Military Academy formally welcomed its Class of 2030 — 367 cadets — as the first PMA cohort eligible to directly commission into the Philippine Coast Guard under Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1 (2025), a structural reform driven by DND Secretary Teodoro to strengthen PCG officer pipelines for WPS operations. PCG Commandant Admiral Gavan described the program as 'a critical gain for seamless coordination in the West Philippine Sea.'
